supersedes: the first v8 recipe (2 palettes x 3 fixed scales {0.7,1.0,1.3} x 2 fixed shifts at 0.4 frame widths x 2 AA), abandoned at 10,538 of 171,384 tiles
why: the fixed 0.4-frame-width shift at scale 1.3 put the window 0.52 base frame widths off centre — off the structure entirely — while the tile kept the location's label. That corrupts only the positive classes (an empty crop labeled 1 is roughly true; labeled 3 or 4 it is a lie) and fights deploy, which reframes to centre content before scoring.
axes: 4 palettes x 3 geometries x 2 AA levels

always_roles.twilight_shifted: deploy-matched; data_v4.NEUTRAL_PALETTE, the pinned scoring instrument and the canonical eval view
always_roles.blue_orange: the vivid companion the human labels were formed through (data/palettes/vivid_blue_orange.json); closes the judge/model presentation gap

palettes.held_out_role: no location may draw these; they are the held-out-palette invariance read at eval time
palettes.draw_scope: PER LOCATION, not per crop — all 4 palettes share the location's 3 geometries, so 24 tiles rest on 6 distinct escape-time fields

identity.role: the deploy composition; present in every (palette, AA) cell

jittered.shift_frac: U(0, 0.1) of the slot frame width

previous_recipe_magnitudes.note: recorded for the first time — these were never written down, only seen
previous_recipe_magnitudes.shift_frac_basis: the SLOT frame width (scale x base), so 0.28/0.40/0.52 base

colormap_library.note: v4-render-batch takes ONE --colormaps path and blue_orange is in neither committed library, so the two committed sources are concatenated verbatim (stops and mirror_needed untouched)

cache_render.note: width/height/jpg_quality are v4-render-batch defaults, unchanged from v4..v8. maxiter is NOT: v4..v8 rendered EVERY tile at the subcommand's flat 8000 regardless of fw — never through auto_maxiter — so the training cache and the deploy crop have never agreed on the cap. v9 emits the production cap per plan row.

maxiter_policy.basis: the SLOT frame width (scale x base), not the location's — a jittered slot gets the cap its own frame resolves
maxiter_policy.residual: x8 covers the MEDIAN convergent multiple (mean 7.7 / median 8.0); the measured tail runs to x24, so the most decorated material stays somewhat clipped. Median-clean, not clean.

executor_note: the plan shares 4 palettes per escape-time field, but v4-render-batch renders each row independently, so that sharing is NOT exploited today — see marginal_cost below

reuse_audit.why: ZERO, and this time the v8 tree IS on disk and IS attributable — the reason is the cap, not durability. Every v8 tile was iterated to a flat maxiter=8000 (v4-render-batch's default; the v8 plan carries no per-row cap), while v9 iterates each slot to auto_maxiter(fw_slot) under the raised policy. Same coordinates, same palette, same filename — DIFFERENT field. Reusing one would put an old-cap tile in a new-cap corpus, which is the exact failure this rebuild exists to remove, so the v9 tree is a separate directory and the v8 tree is left intact as the rollback anchor. (The v4..v7 caches were deleted on 2026-07-29, commit 7068839 — 243,477 JPGs no surviving cache_manifest could attribute to a location.)

trainer_followup: classifier/data_v4.py Loc.palette_renders() asserts exactly 6 palette renders per location and must become 4 (and per-location variable) before a v8 train. canonical() and aa_twin() are unaffected: the identity slot supplies exactly one (twilight_shifted, ss2, scale 1.0, center) row per location.
